keyTerms.definition: The exam's topic shares that the 200 questions match: D1 61, D2 51, D3 41, D4 25, D5 22.
The numbered wrong-answer pattern that each explanation names.
When torn between good options, choose the more managed and more serverless answer.

recall.question: What does the bank contain?
recall.answer: 200 exam-style questions: 52 bonus professional-bar questions (Q141-Q192) and 8 field-research questions (Q193-Q200).

recall.question: What is the Maarek rule of thumb?
recall.answer: Choose the more managed answer, the more serverless answer, and the answer with lower operational overhead.

sections.title: Domain 1: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance (31% of the exam, 61 questions)

keyTerms.definition: The ordered options from cheapest to most expensive; stop at the first that works.
New format, tone, few-shot, and chain-of-thought; no new knowledge.
Retrieval-augmented generation: private, current, or cited facts the model was not trained on.
New behavior baked into weights; labeled data in S3, then usually Provisioned Throughput.

recall.question: A travel company builds a trip planner with four hard constraints: what is the method?
recall.answer: Link each rule to one choice. PoC on Bedrock checks before you spend. Cross-region inference profiles give automatic regional failover.

recall.question: A RAG app returns confident but wrong answers, and the chunks look relevant: where is the failure?
recall.answer: In retrieval, not generation. Split context destroys meaning across chunk boundaries.

sections.title: Domain 2: Implementation and Integration (26% of the exam, 51 questions)

keyTerms.definition: The unified API for the same code across providers with tool use; no exceptions.
The API for embeddings or provider-only parameters; Converse cannot do embeddings.
The required step after any action-group change, or the agent keeps the old DRAFT.

recall.question: An app handles 2 million requests a day with 10x spikes: what is the pattern?
recall.answer: Hybrid. Provisioned Throughput's hourly commitment covers the normal amount. On-demand covers spikes.

recall.question: Provisioned Throughput is bought but the app still throttles: why?
recall.answer: The code calls the base model ID. PT capacity applies only when invocations target the provisioned model ARN.

sections.title: Domain 3: AI Safety, Security, and Governance (20% of the exam, 41 questions)

keyTerms.definition: Toxicity categories plus prompt attack, severity NONE to HIGH.
Subject-area bans in natural language, such as investment advice or diagnoses.
The word in the question stem that picks the control.

recall.question: A bank assistant handles account data under strict regulation: which three controls?
recall.answer: PrivateLink keeps traffic off the public internet. KMS encrypts data at rest. CloudTrail audits who made calls.

recall.question: A hiring assistant shows skew six months after passing fairness tests: what finds it?
recall.answer: Continuous monitoring with alerts. Fairness changes as data drifts, and a launch test is only a snapshot.

sections.title: Domain 4: Operational Efficiency and Optimization for GenAI Applications. This is 12% of the exam. It has 25 questions.

keyTerms.definition: The pricing control matched to traffic shape, not to the buzzword.
Non-interactive bulk work, about 50 percent cheaper.
Route simple queries cheap; escalate hard ones on low confidence.

recall.question: A SaaS company has 8 million chat requests a month, 70 percent simple lookups: what is the method?
recall.answer: Map each fact to a lever. Tiered routing for simple. Prompt caching for the repeated prefix. PT for the baseline.

recall.question: A RAG app has 9-second p99 latency with 7 seconds in retrieval: where do you fix?
recall.answer: Retrieval. Optimized indexes and sharding cut search time.

sections.title: Domain 5: Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting (11% of the exam, 22 questions)

keyTerms.definition: Content handling, API integration, prompt problems, retrieval problems, then capacity vs routing.
The API's error for a request body the provider's schema rejects.
The RAG evaluation triple in the D5 bank map.

recall.question: How do you evaluate third-party answers plus end-to-end app responses?
recall.answer: Bring-your-own-inference. You supply the responses from any model or full application.

recall.question: The provisioned ARN is correct but traffic 3x still throttles: what is wrong?
recall.answer: Capacity, not routing. Add units for a higher sustained baseline.

sections.title: Bonus Professional-Bar Practice Questions (52 questions, Q141-Q192)

keyTerms.definition: The bonus questions use wrong answers that seem correct.
The bonus questions pair harder scenarios with plausible-looking wrong answers.

recall.question: Three needs: strict 4-step format, a behavior change, a high-volume narrow classifier: what is the method?
recall.answer: Apply the customization ladder three times. The narrow classifier is a distillation target.

recall.question: Agent payments over $10,000 need a finance approver: what gives the long wait?
recall.answer: Step Functions with a callback task token, with timeout and automatic escalation.

sections.title: Field Research Questions: 2026 passer-report patterns (8 questions, Q193-Q200)

keyTerms.definition: September 2026 reports showing the newest patterns AWS uses.
These patterns are the ones the main bank underweights; the field questions target them.

recall.question: Teams must alert on-call before hitting the context limit: what is the method?
recall.answer: Estimate tokens client-side before the call. Only pre-call estimation acts before the failure.

recall.question: Staff must know when bullying language appears in a tutoring chatbot: which mode?
recall.answer: Detect mode. It runs the classifier and reports the verdict without refusing the message.

sections.title: How the 75-question mock maps to the real exam. Score 80 percent or more under timed conditions before you book.Source: original figure for the AWS AIP-C01 Study Guide. How to read this diagram. Take the mock in one sitting: 75 questions in 180 minutes. Count one point per question only if you picked every correct option and nothing else. At 80 percent or more (60 of 75), book the exam. Below 70 percent, revisit the domains you missed most. Re-attempt their bank questions, then take the mock again. 75-Question Full Mock Exam

keyTerms.definition: 75 questions in 180 minutes at the real domain weights.
The dress-rehearsal rule: one sitting, and do not open the answers.

recall.question: When do you book the real exam?
recall.answer: At 80 percent or more (60 of 75) under timed conditions.

recall.question: What if you score below 70 percent?
recall.answer: Revisit the domains you missed most, re-attempt their bank questions, then take the mock again.

keyTerms.definition: The grading step after the mock exam is finished.
The answer table, with a link back to the full explanation for each missed question.

recall.question: How do you use the answer key?
recall.answer: Grade the mock here. Then follow the link to the full explanation for any question you missed.

sections.title: The scoring guide as a ruler. Below 52, revisit your weak domains. 52 to 60 is borderline. 60 or more means ready.Source: original figure for the AWS AIP-C01 Study Guide. Scoring Guide

keyTerms.definition: What the scoring guide changes your mock score into.
The real exam's 100 to 1000 score scale.

recall.question: What do the score bands mean?
recall.answer: Below 52, revisit your weak domains. 52 to 60 is borderline. 60 or more means ready.
